2027 Toyota Tacoma Is Mostly a Carryover, Minor Changes Cause Tiny $180 Price Bump
17 photos
Photo: Toyota
Based on when it was first released, the current generation Toyota Tacoma, the fourth, is about one-third of the way through its life cycle. This means we still have a few more years of minor nips and tucks before a major change comes along.
Exactly that's what we got this week, after the Japanese carmaker presented the 2027 model year version of the pickup truck. With these minor changes also comes a slight price bump, one that's not likely to deter customers in any way.
What Toyota focused on this time was making the package structure of the sales champion of the mid-size pickup segment, as it calls it, easier to understand and use. There are no changes to powertrain or other mechanical components.
The most noteworthy enhancements have to do with the TRD Upgrade Package and TRD Premium Package. The former now offers from the get-go the 14-inch multimedia display, while when it comes to the latter, the same screen is now offered as a standalone option, something that should lower the price of the overall package.
The revised Tacoma also throws in a power driver's seat for all four-door trims SR5 and above, and the SR5 grade is now propped on dark silver-finish alloy wheels. Last but not least, a new color called HoneyComb has been added to the TRD Pro.
Otherwise, the pickup truck continues to be the same versatile self. Built on the TNGA-F platform that's also used by the Tundra, Land Cruiser, and Sequoia, it relies on two powertrain choices to go about its business.
The first is the entry-level i-FORCE that relies on a 2.4-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine capable of delivering 278 horsepower and 317 lb.-ft. of torque.
The star of this rather limited lineup, however, is the i-FORCE MAX Hybrid, which throws in a 2.4-liter turbo engine working in conjunction with a 48-hp electric motor installed inside the eight-speed automatic transmission.
The combined output of this setup is rated at 326 horsepower and 465 lb.-ft. of torque, numbers that make it the most capable, torque-wise, ever made in the Tacoma family. This engine is, however, not meant for all the grades available.
The 2027 Toyota Tacoma will be offered in SR, SR5, TRD PreRunner, TRD Sport, TRD Off-Road, Limited, TRD Pro, and Trailhunter trims, with either a Double Cab or XtraCab cabin and a choice between a 5- or 6-foot bed.
The hybrid powertrain is only available from the get-go on the TRD Pro and Trailhunter, and optionally on the TRD Sport, TRD Off-Road, and Limited.
I said earlier the price hike is not that great. The current 2026 Tacoma sells from $32,545, while the 2027 version will retail for just $180 more, $32,725. The truck is already listed on Toyota's North American configurators.
